Compute neutrality test statistics

Source: R/neutrality.R
calcNeutralityTests.Rd

Generic for computing neutrality tests from within-host variant data. Methods should return a DataFrame with one row per sample.

Calculates neutrality test statistics per sample from a WithinHostExperiment. Implements Tajima's D (Tajima 1989) and Fu's Fs (Fu 1997), adapted for deep sequencing iSNV data.

Usage

calcNeutralityTests(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment'
calcNeutralityTests(
  x,
  indices = c("tajimaD", "fusFs"),
  usePassedOnly = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment.

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

indices

Character vector. Which tests to compute: "tajimaD", "fusFs" (default: both).

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only use variants where qcPass == TRUE.

Value

A DataFrame of neutrality statistics.

A DataFrame with one row per sample and columns sample_id, n_sites (the number of segregating sites each statistic rests on, that is, the sites at which the sample's frequency after QC lies strictly between 0 and 1; a frequency of 0, or of 1, a fixed difference from the reference, is not segregating within the host) and one column per requested test. With \(n\) the effective sample size, the sample's median depth capped at 100, a value is NA in four cases (see tajimaD and fusFs): Tajima's D when n_sites is below three, or when \(n\) is below four; Fu's Fs when n_sites is 0, or when n_sites + 1 exceeds \(n\), which is the case for every sample with 100 or more segregating sites. For each case that occurs, one warning names how many samples it affected.

Details

No genome length is needed. Both statistics depend on the nucleotide diversity summed over the genome, \(\hat{\pi} L\), which is computed directly from the frequencies, so a per-site value would only be multiplied back by the length it was divided by.

Fu's Fs sets the number of haplotypes to n_sites + 1, the infinite-sites maximum, as fusFs explains. It therefore carries no haplotype information, depends only on n_sites, the effective sample size and \(\hat{\pi} L\), and is pushed below 0 under neutrality, increasingly so as \(\theta\) grows (about -7 at \(\theta = 5\) with \(n = 100\), near 0 at \(\theta\) of 1 or less); a negative value is not evidence of expansion.

References

Tajima F (1989). Statistical method for testing the neutral mutation hypothesis by DNA polymorphism. Genetics 123:585-595.

Fu YX (1997). Statistical tests of neutrality of mutations against population growth, hitchhiking and background selection. Genetics 147:915-925.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")
calcNeutralityTests(whe)
#> DataFrame with 1 row and 4 columns
#>     sample_id   n_sites   tajimaD     fusFs
#>   <character> <integer> <numeric> <numeric>
#> 1       donor        15   1.61544 -0.382119
